recommended_approach: Use a Mantaflow gas sim (Domain + Flow, optionally Effectors) to generate voxel grids (at minimum density + temperature/flame), then render the Domain with volume shading driven by those attributes. For blackbody fire, the Blender Manual recommends using the Principled Volume shader’s Blackbody/Temperature inputs (or a custom volume setup) and feeding it the simulation’s temperature attribute (typically named “temperature”) while using the density grid (typically “density”) to shape the volume.

simulation_workflow: Create a Fluid Domain (simulation bounds + global sim settings)
Create one or more Flow objects (emission source)
Add Effectors if needed (to shape/deflect the plume)
Assign a material to the Domain that uses volume attributes for shading
Bake the Cache to generate final simulation data

volume_attributes_for_shading.color_attribute_name: color (typical volume grid for smoke coloring)
volume_attributes_for_shading.temperature_attribute_name: temperature (typical volume grid for temperature / fire blackbody)
volume_attributes_for_shading.flame_output: Volume Info node exposes a scalar Flame output representing fire density
volume_attributes_for_shading.temperature_output_mapping: Volume Info node Temperature output: values 0–1 map to 0–1000 kelvin

principled_volume_blackbody.blackbody_intensity: Set Blackbody Intensity to 1 for physically accurate intensity (manual recommendation)
principled_volume_blackbody.temperature_input: Use Temperature (kelvin) and/or Temperature Attribute (typically “temperature”)—higher values emit more
principled_volume_blackbody.density_input: Use Density and/or Density Attribute (typically “density”) to control volume thickness
principled_volume_blackbody.emission_controls: Principled Volume includes Emission Strength, Emission Color, and Blackbody Tint for artistic control

warnings: Mantaflow workflow requirement: you need at least one Domain and one Flow, and the Domain must exist before baking.
Save the blend-file before baking the fluid cache (manual workflow note).
For attribute-driven fire shading, ensure your shader reads the correct grid names (commonly “density” and “temperature”); mismatched names can result in missing/incorrect emission.
If using the Volume Info node’s Temperature output for blackbody, note it is normalized (0–1) and maps to 0–1000 K; you may need to scale/remap depending on the look you want.
alternative_approaches: Instead of Principled Volume, build a custom volume shader by combining Volume Absorption/Volume Scatter/Emission and fetch simulation grids via Attribute nodes (manual: Volume Components).
Use the Volume Info node outputs (Flame/Temperature/Density) to drive a Blackbody node or custom emission logic, rather than relying solely on Principled Volume’s built-in attribute fields.
